dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts small business concerns seeking federal contracts and federal administrative agencies involved in dissemination.
dimensions.evidence: assist small business concerns in strengthening the cybersecurity infrastructure of such concerns and implementing cybersecurity best practices.

dimensions.assessment: Provides informational and compliance resources rather than imposing new mandatory regulations or operational changes.
dimensions.evidence: provide information and resources to a small business concern seeking to enter into a contract with the Federal Government

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal appropriations or economic cost figures are mentioned in the text.
Amends agency outreach and reporting duties by requiring coordination between the SBA, CISA, and NIST.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator of the Small Business Administration, in consultation with the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology, shall develop and disseminate information

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing outreach obligations and an annual reporting requirement to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the Administrator shall submit to Congress a report

missing_information: Funding levels or authorized budget amounts for carrying out the dissemination and reporting
Specific metrics for measuring small business adoption of the provided resources
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Small Business Administration to develop and distribute cybersecurity information and resources, particularly regarding certification programs for small businesses seeking federal contracts. It affects federal agency dissemination duties and small businesses engaging in federal contracting, but does not alter statutory compliance mandates or create major new spending programs.
